title: Authorization Lifecycle and Procurement Patterns Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates company-wide patterns for authorization lifecycles, change approvals, data handling during procurement, vendor relationship checkpoints, and travel allowances. It is intended for managers, approvers, finance partners, security reviewers, and people-ops staff who operate or approve access, purchases, and vendor onboarding.

Scope

- Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with Redwood systems or purchasing on behalf of the company.
- Covers: access requests and deprovisioning, change-management approvals for infrastructure and service procurement, data classification applied to vendor contracts, expense and travel allowances, and operational templates used by approvers.

Definitions

- Authorization lifecycle: request → approval → provisioning → periodic review → deprovisioning.
- Owner: the functional manager who is accountable for a role or resource.
- Approver: the person empowered to grant access or spend (could be manager, director, finance, or security).
- Sensitive data: any data marked Confidential or Restricted under Data Management policy.

1) Access & Permissions (Authorization Lifecycle)

Objective: enforce least privilege while keeping onboarding friction low for product and infra teams.

Key rules and roles:

- Role-based groups are the primary authorization units (e.g., eng-deploy, analytics-read, oncall-sre).
- Temporary elevated access is granted via time-bound access tickets (max 72 hours for standard escalations, 8 hours for emergency break-glass).
- All access requests must record business justification and ticket reference in the provisioning audit entry.

Approval matrix (summary):

| Resource type | Default approver | Secondary approver | Max duration | Auto-expiry |
|---------------|------------------|---------------------|--------------|------------|
| Production cluster access | Engineering manager (owner) | SRE lead | 30 days | yes |
| Billing/finance console | Finance manager | Head of Ops | 90 days | yes |
| Sensitive dataset access | Data owner | Security reviewer | 14 days | yes |
| Vendor portal access | Vendor manager | Security | per contract | yes |

Provisioning process (step-by-step):

1. Submit request using the Access Request form (internal template: Access Request v2) with business justification and ticket link.
2. System auto-assigns default approver based on resource tagged owner; approver receives email + Slack notice.
3. Approver either Approve / Request changes / Reject in 48 hours. If no action, escalation to approver's manager after 48 hours.
4. On approval, IAM automation provisions role membership and logs activity to the audit index.
5. Provisioned access is tagged with an expiry date matching the request duration; reminders are sent 7 and 2 days before expiry.

Deprovisioning and periodic review:

- Automated monthly review: owners receive a digest listing active memberships; they must certify or request continued access.
- Immediate deprovision is triggered on offboarding via HR signals (HR to IAM webhook).
- Emergency revocation: security can revoke any membership immediately; follow-up post-incident review required.

2) Change Management (for Procurement and Infra Changes)

Policy summary:

- Any change that impacts production latency, cost > $5,000/month, or data residency must go through Change Review Board (CRB).
- Low-risk changes (configuration flips with documented rollback < 15 minutes) may use the standard change flow and do not require full CRB if automated tests pass.

Change request template (required fields):

- Change owner, proposed window, rollback plan, monitoring playbook, estimated cost delta, data impact assessment, security signoff.

CRB cadence and SLAs:

- CRB meets twice weekly; requests submitted at least 72 hours prior for normal review.
- Emergency changes documented within 24 hours and reviewed retroactively at next CRB.

3) Data Management Considerations During Procurement

- Classify data flows before any vendor evaluation. If vendor will process Confidential or Restricted data, involve Security and Legal before RFP.
- Minimum contractual protections for Restricted: encryption at rest+in transit, SOC 2 or ISO 27001 evidence, breach notification within 72 hours, right to audit clause.

Checklist for vendor data handling (procurement must attach to PO):

- Data classification confirmation (Public | Internal | Confidential | Restricted).
- Required certifications (SOC2 / ISO / GDPR adequacy).
- Data flow diagram showing locations and subprocessors.
- Retention and deletion commitments.

4) Procurement & Expenses Patterns

Spending thresholds and approval paths:

- <$2,500: individual contributors may spend within card limits with manager notification.
- $2,500–$25,000: manager approval + finance validation (budget check).
- >$25,000: director-level approval + procurement engagement; formal RFP for >$100,000.

Preferred vendor onboarding steps (summary):

1. PO request submitted via Procurement portal with cost center and GL code.
2. Finance validates budget and issues provisional approval within 2 business days.
3. For vendors that will handle company data, Security must sign off before contract execution.
4. Procurement issues PO and finance confirms payment terms in the contract record.

Credit card and expense policy highlights:

- Business meals must include attendee list and business purpose.
- Travel expenses follow the Travel Allowances section below; luxury upgrades are non-reimbursable unless pre-approved by director.
- Receipts required for expenses > $25. Missing receipts require written manager approval.

5) Vendor Management and Relationships

Onboarding gates:

- Finance: tax forms and payment terms.
- Legal: contract template signed with required clauses (IP, confidentiality, indemnification).
- Security: data handling & technical access review.
- Procurement: vendor scoring and PO issuance.

Ongoing vendor health checks (quarterly):

- SLA attainment, security posture changes, spend versus contractual commitment, and single-point-of-failure analysis.
- High-risk vendors (access to Restricted data or >$250k annual spend) require semi-annual executive review.

Exit and offboarding rules:

- Revoke all technical access within 48 hours of contract end.
- Confirm data deletion or hand-off as per contract; collect certificate of deletion when applicable.

6) Travel Policy and Allowances (summary)

- Purpose: cover reasonable costs that enable business outcomes while managing spend predictably.
- Booking: Redwood partners with preferred travel vendor; preferred fares should be used for bookings > 3 days in advance.

Allowances and limits:

- Economy flights up to $800 domestically; up to $1,500 for trans-continental economy. Business class permitted for flights > 8 hours only with director approval.
- Hotel: up to $250/night in major metro areas; exceptions require manager pre-approval.
- Per diem: $60/day for domestic day travel.

Expense submission timeline:

- Submit within 10 business days of trip end. Finance will flag late submissions to managers.

7) Templates & Forms (location and usage)

- Access Request v2 (template id: AR-V2): used for all role and resource requests.
- Procurement PO template (P0-Standard): pre-filled fields: cost center, GL code, vendor id, payment terms.
- Vendor Security Intake (VSI-1): questionnaire used for data handling and certifications.

CLI & automation snippets

- Example: generate an access ticket via CLI (internal tool: rdxctl)

  rdxctl access request --resource "project/prod-cluster" --role "eng-deploy" \\n    --justification "Hotfix rollout" --duration 72h --owner "alice@redwood.ai"

- Example: IAM policy JSON (short) to tag an ephemeral role with expiry label:

  {
    \"role\": \"eng-deploy-ephemeral\",
    \"expiry\": \"2029-02-01T00:00:00Z\",
    \"request_ticket\": \"RDW-4231\"
  }

8) Audit checklist and KPIs

Quarterly audit items:

- 100% of terminated employees deprovisioned within 24 hours. Target: 100%.
- Access certification completion rate: 95% per team per quarter.
- Number of emergency break-glass events and time to remediation. Target: <3 per quarter.

Reporting cadence and dashboards:

- Weekly automation report: new access granted, pending approvals >48h, and upcoming expiries.
- Monthly spend vs. PO report for vendors > $10k/month.

9) Governance, Escalation, and Ownership

- People-ops: owner of the authorization lifecycle process and onboarding templates.
- Finance & Procurement: owner of the spend controls and PO lifecycle.
- Security: owner of the Sensitive data treatment and vendor technical assessments.

Escalation flow:

1. If an approver is unresponsive for 48 hours, escalate to approver's manager.
2. If the approver and manager are both unavailable for 72 hours and access is business-critical, open an emergency CRB ticket.
